subject: gk
question: The Constitution (42ⁿd Amendment) Act, 1976, Chapter IV-A introduced a code of ten _____________ for citizens.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Duties**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, enacted in **1976**, introduced the concept of Fundamental Duties.
 
• These duties are outlined in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution under Article **51A**.
 
• Originally, the amendment included **ten Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens.
 
• These duties were added based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
• One more duty was added later, making the total **eleven Fundamental Duties** currently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union (USSR).
 
• They serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they should also perform their duties towards the country.
 
• They are not enforceable by law, but they are considered essential for promoting a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• Some examples include respecting the national symbols, cherishing the heritage, and protecting the environment.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**
 
 
• These principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution and are aimed at guiding the state in policy-making and legislation.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts.
 
• They were inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Examples include provisions for adequate livelihood, equal pay for equal work, and promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution and are considered essential for the overall development of individuals.
 
• They are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the courts for the enforcement of these rights.
 
• Examples include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• These rights are essential for the protection of individual liberty and democratic principles in the country.
